## PART 1 – Hunk-by-hunk walk

**Hunk 1 (python/dashboard/templates/index.html):** no correctness change.
The "Send to Chat" handler is intentionally reduced from a full-context dump to `id + title`; the comment and the new `read_task`/`search_tasks` tools in `local-tool-client.js` are the documented replacement path. No caller of `sendTextToChat` or the `/api/chat/inject` endpoint depends on the removed fields being present in the injected text.

**Hunk 2 (src/grep-codebase-tool.js):** SUSPECT – the local `lineMatches` implementation is deleted and replaced by `require('./text-match.js')`. The diff does not show the body of `text-match.js` (it is in the truncated portion), so I cannot confirm the new implementation is semantically identical (exact-substring fast-path → multi-token case-insensitive fallback, `tokens.length < 2` guard). If the new version drops the fast-path or changes the token-splitting, every existing `grepCodebase` call site silently gets different match results. **UNKNOWN** pending the full file.

**Hunk 3 (src/grep-codebase-tool.js):** no correctness change.
Comment-only update explaining the move of `lineMatches`; no executable code altered.

**Hunk 4 (src/local-tool-client.js – imports):** no correctness change.
Two new `require` lines for `task-anywhere.js` and `text-match.js`; both files are added in this same commit. No existing symbol's binding is altered.

**Hunk 5 (src/local-tool-client.js – new functions `taskSummary`, `READ_TASK_SECTIONS`, `formatTaskHistory`, `windowSectionText`, `readTaskTool`, `candidateTaskFiles`, `archivedTaskFiles`, `searchTasksTool`):** SUSPECT – two issues in the new `windowSectionText` helper:

1. **Truncation / `nextOffset` skip.** When `slice.length > MAX_READ_FILE_CHARS`, the content is cut at the character limit, but `nextOffset` is still computed as `endLine + 1` (the *un-truncated* end). A caller that pages forward with that `nextOffset` will silently skip every line between the character-cut point and `endLine`. The `returnedThrough` variable is set to `off` (i.e. the start line), making the notice read "showing lines 1-1 of N" which is misleading and confirms the bookkeeping is inconsistent.

2. **`returnedThrough` is wrong on truncation.** It should reflect the last line actually visible, but it is set to `off` (the first line), so the paging notice is incorrect. This is new code (no "before" state), so it is not a regression, but it is a correctness defect in the new path.

The remaining new functions (`taskSummary`, `readTaskTool`, `searchTasksTool`, `candidateTaskFiles`, `archivedTaskFiles`) are new; no prior behaviour is displaced. `searchTasksTool` calls `lineMatches(haystack, query)` with the same argument order the old local function used, so if `text-match.js` preserves that order (UNKNOWN per Hunk 2), the call is correct.

**Hunks 6–12 (not shown in the truncated diff):** UNKNOWN – cannot evaluate.

**New files `src/task-anywhere.js`, `src/task-anywhere.test.js`, `src/text-match.js`:** UNKNOWN – full content not present in the visible hunks.

---

## PART 2 – Changed public symbols / callers to locate

The diff **removes** the local `lineMatches` from `grep-codebase-tool.js` and re-exports it from `text-match.js`. Any file that previously did `require('./grep-codebase-tool.js')` and used `lineMatches` directly (rather than through `grepCodebase`) would break. The diff only shows `grep-codebase-tool.js` and `local-tool-client.js` importing it, but a repo-wide check is warranted.

The diff also **adds** new exports to `local-tool-client.js` (`readTaskTool`, `searchTasksTool`, `taskSummary`, `candidateTaskFiles`, `archivedTaskFiles`, `windowSectionText`, `READ_TASK_SECTIONS`, `MAX_SEARCH_TASK_RESULTS`, `formatTaskHistory`) and to `task-anywhere.js` (`findTaskAnywhere`, `QUEUE_STATES`). These are new symbols with no prior callers, so no caller-update check is needed.

The only symbol whose **contract** changed (moved to a different module) is:

QUERY: lineMatches

File: src/local-tool-client.js
Line: hunk @@ -170,24 +172,222 @@ (function `windowSectionText`)
Severity: med
Regression: New helper `windowSectionText` (introduced in this diff; did not exist before) computes `nextOffset` from the un-truncated line-window end, so after the character-limit truncation fires, a caller that pages forward with the returned `nextOffset` silently skips every line that was inside the window but cut off by the character limit; `returnedThrough` is also set to `off` (the start line) rather than the last line actually visible, making the paging notice factually wrong.
Failure scenario: A task JSON in `queue/done/` has `planResponse` = `"A

N
O
P"` (16 lines). The model calls `read_task` with `{ taskId: "abc123", section: "plan" }` (no offset/limit, so `off=1`, `lim=READ_FILE_DEFAULT_LINES`). `endLine = 16`. The joined slice is 31 chars. If `MAX_READ_FILE_CHARS` is, say, 10, the slice is cut to `"A
B
C
D
E
F
G
...[truncated…]"`, `truncated=true`, `returnedThrough = off = 1`, `nextOffset = 16 < 16 → null` (no skip here because the window reaches the end). Now use a smaller window: `limit = 5`. `endLine = 5`, slice = `"A
B
C
D
E"` (9 chars). With `MAX_READ_FILE_CHARS = 5`, the slice is cut to `"A
B
C
...[truncated…]"`, `truncated = true`, `returnedThrough = 1`, `nextOffset = 5 < 16 → 6`. The notice reads *"showing lines 1-1 of 16. Re-call with offset=6 for the next window."* The content actually contains parts of lines 1–3, but the notice claims only line 1 was shown, and the suggested next offset (6) skips lines 4 and 5 ("D" and "E"), which the caller will never retrieve by following the tool's own paging advice.
Fix sketch: When `truncated` is true, compute `returnedThrough` as the index of the last `
` in the truncated `slice` (i.e. `slice.lastIndexOf('
') + 1`, 1-based) and set `nextOffset` to `returnedThrough + 1` instead of `endLine + 1`, so the caller resumes at the first line that was actually cut off rather than jumping past the entire un-truncated window.
